ctx.en: "He plagiarised it and now he's giving an acceptance speech? Utterly shameless."

ctx.s: 不正[ふせい]を指摘[してき]されても平然[へいぜん]としている{厚顔無恥[こうがんむち]}な態度[たいど]に、批判[ひはん]が集[あつ]まった。
ctx.en: His brazen unconcern, even after the wrongdoing was exposed, drew a storm of criticism.

ctx.s: 会社[かいしゃ]のお金[かね]を使[つか]い込[こ]んでおきながら退職金[たいしょくきん]を要求[ようきゅう]するとは、{厚顔無恥[こうがんむち]}としか言[い]いようがない。
ctx.en: Embezzling the company's money and then demanding a retirement payout: there is no word for it but shameless.

bad.en: (meant: he is confident and never gets nervous in front of crowds)
bad.why: It is a severe insult for shameless conduct, not praise for confidence; say monooji shinai or doudou to shite iru.

bad.s: 私[わたし]は歴史[れきし]については{厚顔無恥[こうがんむち]}です。
bad.en: (meant: I know nothing about history)
bad.why: Its muchi means 'without shame', not the homophone meaning 'without knowledge'; for ignorance say kuwashiku nai.

lit: writing the play oneself and acting in it oneself

use.how: Xは自作自演だった, 自作自演の事件: exposing an incident, threat or show of support that the person secretly staged. Literally, performing one's own composition.

near.diff: 自画自賛 openly praises one's own work; 自作自演 secretly fakes an event or support and passes it off as real.

cue: A shop owner reports a break-in to claim insurance, but the security camera shows the owner smashing the window. What was the 'break-in'?

ctx.s: その脅迫状[きょうはくじょう]は、本人[ほんにん]の{自作自演[じさくじえん]}だった。
ctx.en: The threatening letter turned out to have been written by its supposed target.

ctx.en: "Weren't all these reviews written by the same person?" "Maybe the shop wrote them itself."

ctx.en: The theft turned out to have been staged by the owner to claim the insurance.

ctx.en: He praised his own posts while pretending to be someone else, and got caught faking it.

bad.en: (meant: I live alone, so I do all the cooking and cleaning myself)
bad.why: It implies a faked, staged event; doing your own chores is jibun de yaru.
